items.stem: You need to hide part of a layer but keep the option to bring it back later. Which is the MOST non-destructive approach?

options.text: Add a layer mask and paint the area black
options.rationale: Correct: a layer mask hides pixels reversibly without deleting them.

options.text: Select the area and press Delete

options.rationale: Flattening is destructive and removes layer flexibility.
Resolution changes do not hide a region of a layer.

items.explanation: Correct: a layer mask hides pixels reversibly without deleting them.

items.stem: Which colour mode is generally correct when preparing an image for commercial print?

options.rationale: Correct: commercial print presses use CMYK inks.
sRGB is a web/screen colour space, not for press output.
Grayscale discards colour and is only for monochrome output.
Indexed colour limits the palette and is used for some web GIFs, not print.

items.explanation: Correct: commercial print presses use CMYK inks.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep a retouching workflow non-destructive?

options.text: Use adjustment layers instead of direct image adjustments
options.rationale: Correct: adjustment layers can be edited or removed at any time.

options.text: Convert layers to smart objects before filtering
options.rationale: Correct: smart objects preserve the original and allow re-editable smart filters.

options.text: Apply filters directly to the flattened base layer
options.rationale: That bakes in the effect destructively.

options.text: Save only as a flattened JPEG
options.rationale: A flattened JPEG discards layers and masks.

items.explanation: Correct: adjustment layers can be edited or removed at any time.
